chunks: "I'd go through it in layers, starting with the things the SoC can't boot without.

Power first: the SoC needs several rails, say a low-voltage core rail, an I/O rail, and DRAM supplies, usually from a PMIC or a set of buck converters and LDOs, with the right sequencing and decoupling capacitors at every power pin group.
If it's battery powered, add a charger and fuel gauge.
Second, clocks and reset: a crystal or oscillator for the main clock, usually 24 or 26 megahertz, plus a 32 kilohertz crystal for the RTC, and a reset supervisor or at least a defined power-on reset.
Third, memory: if it's an application processor, external LPDDR or DDR for working memory and flash, eMMC or SD for storage and boot code. MCUs often have these on-chip.

Fourth, the I/O side: Ethernet PHY if the SoC only has a MAC, USB connectors and protection, Wi-Fi or cellular modules, level shifters between voltage domains, and ESD protection on anything that leaves the board.
Then the application stuff: sensors, display, audio codec, buttons, LEDs. And bring-up needs a debug header or JTAG/SWD, boot-mode straps, test points, and the thermal solution.
The board design, stackup and layout for DDR and high-speed pairs matter as much as the part list."
